restrictions: Classical 256-bit word RAM with 64 registers and a fresh independent uniform random-word primitive; constant-address loads/stores take the address as an instruction operand (sensitivity in proof Section 6).

One batch of Q (a multiple of 256, ~0.9943*2^128) independent uniform 64-byte messages generated directly in bitsliced form, 256 messages per block; each block hashed by a counted straight-line bitsliced program for the complete 6-round SHA3-256 sponge evaluated in ordinary word operations (62,859 measured ops/block, round-mixing (theta) folded into the producing round); digests transposed to one word per message and XORed with a fixed public mask POL.

Unconditional generic birthday: key-index LSD radix sort (86/85/85-bit digits, 3 passes, histograms fused into generation) of (masked digest, index) pairs, adjacent scan halting at the first equal pair; every output re-verified with the target permutation.

Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge: rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06, prefix rounds 0 through 5, all 256 output bits. Heuristics empty. Visible spare on every hot path (block program 63,500 charged vs 62,859 measured; record 28 vs 25; scatter 15/16/15 vs 12/13/12; scan 7 vs 5). No cryptanalytic weakness of SHA3 claimed.
